question.general_feedback:
Thermometer comparison:

TypeRange (°C)Suitable Use
Mercury-in-glass (laboratory)−10 to 110 °CGeneral laboratory temperature measurements
Clinical35 to 42 °CMeasuring human body temperature
Thermocouple−200 to 1500 °C (very wide)Measuring very high or very low temperatures (e.g. furnaces, flames, industrial processes)

Key points:

  • Mercury-in-glass: thermometric property is expansion of mercury. The narrow range makes it unsuitable for very high temperatures.
  • Clinical: narrow range centred on normal body temp (37 °C); has a constriction to hold the reading after removal from patient.
  • Thermocouple: thermometric property is EMF (voltage) produced at the hot junction; extremely wide range; responds rapidly; gives electrical output.

steps.label:
Three thermometer types: Mercury-in-glass | Clinical | Thermocouple
Key properties: thermometric property, temperature range, suitable use
Complete all 5 missing cells in the thermometer table. (5 marks)

fields.label: Range of mercury-in-glass thermometer = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Mercury-in-glass thermometers typically cover −10 °C to 110 °C (some laboratory versions extend further but the standard CSEC range is approx. −10 to 110).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Mercury-in-glass (laboratory) thermometer range: approximately −10 °C to 110 °C. It cannot measure temperatures above the boiling point of mercury (~357 °C) or below its freezing point (~−39 °C). The CSEC standard quoted range is −10 °C to 110 °C.

fields.label: Suitable use for mercury-in-glass thermometer = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Mercury-in-glass is used for general laboratory temperature measurements where temperatures are within its range.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Mercury-in-glass thermometers are used for general laboratory temperature measurements. They are NOT suitable for body temperature (too slow/not self-reading), very high temperatures (above 357°C), or very low temperatures.

options.Measuring very high or very low temperat: Measuring very high or very low temperatures

fields.label: Suitable use for clinical thermometer = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: The clinical thermometer is specifically designed for measuring human body temperature (35–42 °C).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Clinical thermometers are designed specifically to measure human body temperature. Their narrow range (35–42 °C) is centred on the normal body temperature of 37 °C. The constriction in the tube holds the mercury reading after removal from the patient.

options.Measuring very high or very low temperat: Measuring very high or very low temperatures

fields.label: Range of thermocouple thermometer = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Thermocouple thermometers have a very wide range, typically −200 °C to 1500 °C (or beyond for specialised types).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Thermocouple thermometers have a very wide temperature range, typically from about −200 °C to +1500 °C. This is far greater than mercury-in-glass (−10 to 110 °C) or clinical (35 to 42 °C) thermometers.

fields.label: Suitable use for thermocouple thermometer = _____
fields.expected: Measuring very high or very low temperatures
fields.diagnostic_hint: Thermocouples are used for measuring very high or very low temperatures that are outside the range of other thermometers — e.g., furnaces, flames, industrial processes, cryogenic experiments.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Thermocouple thermometers are suitable for measuring very high temperatures (e.g. furnaces, flames, molten metals) or very low temperatures (e.g. liquid nitrogen research) due to their extremely wide range. Their small junction size and fast response also make them suitable for localised and rapidly changing temperatures.
